modules.intro: Everything you wrote at the five machines, captured here so it is graded on what it says.
modules.title: Your five station records
modules.aiNote: These were written at the machine. Nothing here is generated or rewritten by AI.

blocks.content:
Photograph the pages you wrote at each station and upload them here. Five pages, one per station.

**Take the photo flat, straight on, in good light.** If the page is not readable, it does not count. Check each photo before you upload it.

**What a station record has to show.** For each station:

- The machine and the part.
- The settings you actually used. Speed, feed, depth, power, passes, whatever that machine has. As used, not as planned.
- The tool or workholding you chose. You explain why in your presentation, not here.
- **What happened.** A problem, a mistake, a measurement that came out wrong, or something you changed mid-cut. This is the part that gets graded here.

**Graded on what the records say, not on how neat they are.** Handwriting and layout are scored once, in the Documentation Check, and never here.

Missing a page? Write it now from memory and mark it as written late. A late honest record beats a blank.

items: Five pages uploaded, one per station
Each record names the machine and the part
Each record has the settings I actually used
Each record names the tool or workholding I used
Each record names something specific that happened: a problem, a mistake, a measurement that came out wrong, or a change mid-cut

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Five station pages uploaded, every one readable, and every one names its machine and its part.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Five pages uploaded with one hard to read, or one missing its machine or part.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Three or four stations captured.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Two stations or fewer captured.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: All five records carry the settings actually used at that machine and name the tool or workholding used, in terms specific to that machine.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: One of the two is missing from one record, or one record gives planned rather than used values.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: One or both missing from two or three records, or those records name the operation only.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Settings and tooling are absent from most records.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: All five records name something that actually happened at that machine: a problem, a mistake, a measurement that came out wrong, or something changed mid-cut.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Four records name a specific event; one is a general statement.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Two or three records name a specific event.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: One record or none names anything that happened.

modules.intro: The five drawings you made before each part, captured here.
modules.title: Your five drawings
modules.aiNote: You drew these on paper. Nothing here is generated by AI.

blocks.content:
Photograph your five drawings and upload them here. One per part.

Flat, straight on, in good light, dimensions legible.

**The standard has not changed:** someone who has never seen the model could make the part from your drawing. Every dimension needed to manufacture it, every feature.

The topper drawing is your own design sketch with its two constraints marked: the 2.5 inch maximum across, and the 1/4 inch hole at the center.

Changed something between drawing the part and making it? Mark it on the drawing. A drawing that matches the part you actually made beats a clean one that does not.

items: Five drawings uploaded, one per part
Every dimension needed to make the part is on the drawing
My topper drawing shows the 2.5 in limit and the center hole

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Five drawings uploaded and every one is legible.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Five uploaded with one hard to read.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Three or four drawings uploaded.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Two drawings or fewer.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: All five drawings carry every dimension and feature needed to make the part with no guessing, and the topper sketch marks its 2.5 inch limit and its center hole.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: One dimension or feature missing from one drawing, or the topper sketch is missing one of its two constraint marks.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Dimensions or features missing from two or three drawings.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Most drawings could not be used to make the part.

modules.intro: Put it together, photograph it standing, and write down what fit and what did not.
modules.title: Assemble the trophy
modules.aiNote: AI may help you word what you noticed. It may not decide what fit or did not.

blocks.content:
Put the trophy together. All five parts, 1/4-20 hardware, base to topper.

Then photograph it assembled, standing on its own.

**Assembly is a measurement.** If a part does not fit, that is data, and it is the most useful data in the unit. Do not hide it and do not skip it.

Write down what did not fit and why you think it did not. If everything fit the first time, say that, and say which fit was tightest.

You keep this.

blocks.prompt: What did not fit, and why do you think it did not? Name the part and the feature. If everything fit the first time, say so and name the fit that was tightest and what made it tight.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Photo shows the trophy assembled from all five parts and standing on its own.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Trophy is assembled but the photo is unclear or does not show all five parts.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Some parts assembled, or parts shown laid out rather than together.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No assembly photo uploaded.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names the specific part and feature that did not fit, or the tightest fit if all fit, and gives a reason tied to how it was made or measured.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Names the part and feature but the reason is general.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Says something fit or did not without naming the part or feature.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No response.

rubric.criterion: What fit and what did not
